## B. Drift findings

1. **Endpoint ↔ data-model** *(core)* — ✓ `import` writes `collection_snapshots` and
   `collection_issue_transitions`; `compute` reads `collection_*` and writes `computation_measurements` and
   `computation_state_maps`.
2. **Error code ↔ repo error definition** *(core)* — ✓ The repo has no code-level error registry yet
   (`shared.Refusal` arrives in S9); the registry is the closed list in F1 ADR 0007, and all six refusal
   codes match it. `snapshot_invalid` is the contract's proposal, parked (Deferrals 1). Bare codes instead
   of `module.error_name`: deviation by F1 ADR 0007.
3. **Validation ↔ constraint** *(core)* — ✓ `--period` `YYYY-MM` ↔ `period` TEXT `YYYY-MM` (F1 ADR 0006);
   `--version` integer ≥ 1 ↔ `definition_version` INTEGER; `outcome` enum ↔ CHECK
   (`value` | `no_finished_passes`); value absent exactly when `no_finished_passes` ↔ CHECK on `value`.
4. **Entity / AC ↔ endpoint (coverage)** *(supporting)* — ✓ All 4 tables are surfaced (`import`:
   2 collection tables; `compute`: 2 computation tables). All 11 ACs map to a reply: AC-01, AC-01b, AC-02,
   AC-03, AC-08 to `compute` output; AC-04..AC-07, AC-09, AC-10 to refusals; AC-03 defect to exit 4.
   `import` maps to US-04 through AC-07 (the fix the refusal names); it has no user story of its own.
5. **Contract ↔ sequence** *(supporting)* — ✓ (deferred: two error replies the contract needs have no §6
   branch: malformed definitions file (usage error per ADR 0007) and invalid argument values such as
   `--period 2026-13`). Every §6 `alt` branch (flow 1: 3, flow 2: 6, flow 3: 2 + 2) has an exit code and a
   reply.
